answer: Under burst-squared proof-of-work banding, every identity enrolling in the harbor network during the same calendar minute must attach a proof of work whose difficulty equals base_hash_rate times the square of identities joining that minute, with each proof anchored to a distinct vertex in the enrollment graph so duplicates fail. A farmer flooding a hundred identities in one minute pays difficulty 10,000x per proof, about ten thousand seconds each, making bulk enrollment nonlinearly expensive while crystal-clear honest onboarding stays cheap.
